accounts.emailsHint: One row per address your team cares about (work inboxes, billing, recovery). Link them from asset and identity pages.
accounts.vaultPerAssetHint: Vault links live on each asset access (asset → email), not here. Open an asset’s Access tab and use the key icon next to the login email.

graph.title: Dependency map
graph.hint: Drag nodes, scroll to zoom, pan on the background. Use expand (top-right) for fullscreen. Click arrows or nodes for detail cards.

relationHelp.depends_on: The source asset needs the target to work (ordering, DNS, upstream API, etc.).
relationHelp.hosted_on: The source runs on or inside the target (app on VPS, site on hosting).
relationHelp.deployed_from: Deploys or releases originate from the source toward the target environment.
relationHelp.authenticated_by: The source uses the target for login or tokens (OAuth client → identity).
relationHelp.stores_data_in: Persistent data for the source lives in the target (DB, bucket, registry).
relationHelp.sends_email_via: Outbound mail from the source goes through the target (SES, SMTP).
relationHelp.domain_registered_at: Domain ownership is registered with the target registrar.
relationHelp.dns_managed_by: DNS for the source is served or managed by the target.
relationHelp.verified_with: Ownership or delivery verification ties the source to the target.
relationHelp.publishes_to: The source publishes content or builds to the target.
relationHelp.billed_through: Costs for the source are invoiced via the target account.
relationHelp.recovery_depends_on: Recovery or backup of the source depends on the target.
relationHelp.other: Custom relationship — document intent in dependency notes if needed.

checklist.q4: Which YouTube channel and which identities have admin access?
checklist.q5: Search Console property and verification method for northline.example?
checklist.q5hint: Search Console asset (billing identity); domain asset.
checklist.q6: Dependencies: registrar vs DNS vs mailbox vs AWS SES?

checklist.q7: What runs on each VPS, deploy from which repo, SSH vault ref?
checklist.q7hint: VPS + repo assets; deployed_from / hosted_on edges; vault reference.
checklist.q8: Image storage config and consuming app?
checklist.q9: Onboard another developer without sharing passwords?
checklist.q9hint: Create a developer onboarding runbook; export Markdown without pasting secrets.

templates.catalogSubtitle: Preview what each template covers before generating a runbook from your inventory.
templates.howGenerationWorksBody: Hilko fills steps from linked assets, vault ref labels, and config keys—never secret values. Missing inventory shows as “pending” in the generated Markdown.
templates.stepsHint: Order and wording may change after you edit the runbook. Titles below come from the system template.
templates.afterCreateBody: Edit overview and steps, refresh auto blocks from inventory, run an execution, and export Markdown for the new person.

templates.previewEmpty: Add a step title to preview.
templates.deleteWorkspaceDescription: Runbooks already created from this template stay in your workspace; only the reusable template is removed.
templates.workspaceSubtitle: Reusable runbook skeleton for your workspace—fixed Markdown steps you can turn into a runbook for any project.
templates.workspaceHintBody: Chain human steps with Hilko links (Emails, Assets…) and optional inventory blocks. Use **Insert workflow** for flows like changing a registrar contact email.

changeRegistrarEmail.label: Change registrar / admin contact email
changeRegistrarEmail.s1Title: Confirm the new email is valid
changeRegistrarEmail.s1Body: Check inbox access and that the address is acceptable for WHOIS / registrar notifications (not a shared inbox unless policy allows).
changeRegistrarEmail.s2Body: Open [Emails & access](/accounts?tab=emails) and add the address with a short label (e.g. “Northline admin 2025”). Link it to the domain asset if relevant.
changeRegistrarEmail.s3Body: Choose your **Namecheap (or registrar) asset** below, open its admin URL, and set the management / contact email to the new address. Save in the provider UI.
changeRegistrarEmail.s4Body: Confirm the provider shows the new email, resend any verification message, and note the change in the runbook execution.

recordEmail.label: Document a mailbox in Hilko
recordEmail.s1Body: Go to [Emails & access](/accounts?tab=emails). Create the row with purpose (billing, admin, notifications…) — metadata only.
recordEmail.s2Body: On each related [asset](/assets), attach the mailbox under **Emails** so impact search and runbooks stay accurate.

verifyClose.label: Final review step
verifyClose.s1Body:
- [ ] Provider UI matches Hilko
- [ ] No secrets pasted into tickets or runbook notes
- [ ] Next owner knows where to look in Hilko

linkVault.s1Body: Never paste secret values into Hilko. Use [Assets](/assets) → vault hint field or project **Vault references** (labels + URLs only).
linkVault.s2Body: Choose the Bitwarden/1Password item below. Confirm `itemUrl` or location hint is enough for you to find credentials offline.
linkVault.s3Title: Attach to the asset that uses it
linkVault.s3Body: Select the asset (app, server, OAuth client…) and confirm the vault label matches what operators expect in a crisis.

dnsCutover.s1Body: Write new public targets as **config entries** (non-secret). Lower TTL 24–48h before cutover. Note rollback values in execution notes.
dnsCutover.s2Body: Pick your **Cloudflare / DNS asset**, apply the new A/AAAA/CNAME. Do not paste zone secrets into Hilko.
dnsCutover.s3Body: Review dependency map below—mail, hosting, certs—before you declare done.
dnsCutover.s4Body:
- [ ] Site resolves
- [ ] TLS valid
- [ ] Raise TTL after stable window

soloIdentity.s1Body: Open [Identities](/accounts?tab=identities). One row should match the human who actually logs into providers. Delete ghost “Team” identities.
soloIdentity.s2Body: Below: every asset should show **your** identity. Fix [asset](/assets) → Access tabs when a vendor still lists a dead account.
soloIdentity.s3Body: In [Emails & access](/accounts?tab=emails), drop aliases you ignore. Registrar and billing must reach a mailbox you monitor.

soloVacation.s1Title: What breaks if you vanish for a week
soloVacation.s1Body: Skim project assets. Star billing, DNS expiry, and anything without a second human—see [Projects](/projects).
soloVacation.s2Body: Confirm vault refs name the items a helper would need (hosting, domain, PM). Still no secret paste.
soloVacation.s3Body: Export a runbook Markdown, store in PM, leave Hilko as source of truth. Optional: one trusted person gets vault—not shared passwords.

new-developer-onboarding.title: Onboard a new developer
new-developer-onboarding.description: Hand repo and tooling access using individual accounts and vault refs.
new-developer-onboarding.howTo:
Choose the project and dev/staging environment.
Link GitHub repos, OAuth, vault refs, and config entries in inventory first.
Generate the runbook and send the exported README—no shared passwords.

staging-environment-bootstrap.title: Bootstrap staging / dev environment
staging-environment-bootstrap.description: Stand up or rebuild a non-production environment from documented links.
staging-environment-bootstrap.howTo:
Pick the project and the environment you are rebuilding.
Ensure VPS, domain, mail, and storage assets are linked to that environment.
Use the runbook as a checklist while you stand up services; export for the team.

access-handover-checklist.title: Access handover
access-handover-checklist.description: Document who takes over accounts, emails, and roles.
access-handover-checklist.howTo:
Select the project whose ownership is changing.
Update identities, asset roles, emails, and vault refs before generating.
Complete the execution with notes so the next owner has an audit trail in Hilko.

registrar-contact-email-change.title: Change registrar / admin contact email
registrar-contact-email-change.description: Checklist: validate mailbox → Hilko → Namecheap (or registrar) panel → review.
registrar-contact-email-change.howTo:
Pick the project that owns the domain.
Ensure the Namecheap (or registrar) domain asset is linked.
Generate and follow steps; link the specific registrar asset in team templates if you clone this flow.

solo-founder-inventory-audit.title: Solo founder: inventory truth check
solo-founder-inventory-audit.description: One person: identities, roles, mailboxes, and vault refs match reality.
solo-founder-inventory-audit.howTo:
Use when you are the only Hilko user.
Fix identities and roles before exporting.
Clear the verification queue so nothing is fake-“declared”.

solo-vacation-handoff.title: Solo operator: vacation packet
solo-vacation-handoff.description: Before time off: scope, vault, domains, export—for you or one helper.
solo-vacation-handoff.howTo:
No team required.
Complete vault ref labels first.
Export Markdown to your password manager; share access, not passwords.

dns-cutover-checklist.title: DNS cutover to new host
dns-cutover-checklist.description: TTL prep, DNS asset change, dependency check, smoke test.
dns-cutover-checklist.howTo:
Pick project + environment.
Link Cloudflare (or DNS) and hosting assets.
Use when repointing production or staging DNS.

verification.title: Verification in Hilko
verification.lede: Hilko never stores secrets. Verification is how you record that a human checked control or ownership — or that the item is inventory-only until you check.
verification.statusesIntro: Each asset, dependency, and role has one status. The home dashboard counts anything that is not Confirmed yet.

statusBodies.unverified: Not reviewed yet. Typical for new rows or seed/demo data.
statusBodies.declared: You listed it in inventory (wizard, CSV, manual entry) but have not confirmed control.
statusBodies.confirmed_by_human: You or someone on the team checked access, DNS, registrar, or console login and documented how.

verification.methodsIntro: When you confirm control, add a verification record: pick how you checked and optional notes (hostnames, ticket IDs, no secrets). Methods are labels for humans — not automated probes (integrations come in a later phase).

methodBodies.dns_txt: Ownership proved via a DNS TXT record (domain, SES, Google site verification, etc.).
methodBodies.html_file: HTML file uploaded to the site root or host.
methodBodies.meta_tag: Meta tag placed in site HTML.
methodBodies.cname: DNS CNAME points to a provider verification target.
methodBodies.registrar_lock: Checked registrar WHOIS, lock, or auth codes policy.
methodBodies.provider_console: Logged into vendor admin (AWS, Google, GitHub, hosting panel) and confirmed the asset exists.
methodBodies.manual_check: Other documented check (screenshot ref, runbook step, ticket) — describe in the note.
methodBodies.other: Catch-all; still add a short note.

methodExamples.provider_console: e.g. Note: SES region eu-west-1, identity verified

flowSteps.0: Open Home → verification queue or Assets → Needs confirmation.
flowSteps.2: Use “I control this” for a quick console check, or pick a method + evidence note.
flowSteps.3: Status becomes Confirmed; the dashboard count goes down.

verification.flowNote: You can also set status in Overview and save — use Confirmed only when you have actually checked.

onboarding.title: Quick setup
onboarding.subtitle: Map your first project in a few minutes. No passwords or API keys are stored.
onboarding.welcomeBody: Hilko organizes projects, tools, sign-in accounts, and how they connect. This wizard creates your first project and a starter map you can refine later.
onboarding.welcomeList1: Projects group sites, apps, or clients.
onboarding.welcomeList2: You set each resource with its identity, login email, role, and verification in one pass.
onboarding.welcomeList3: You can pause anytime; progress is saved automatically.
onboarding.projectHint: Use your real product or client name. You can add more projects later.
onboarding.websiteUnverified: Domain not verified yet — save without https://
onboarding.websiteHint: When you own the domain, keep https://; otherwise tick unverified until DNS is confirmed.
onboarding.toolsHint: Pick what you use today. Optional — skip if you prefer to add things manually.
onboarding.accountsHint: Who signs in to each provider? Use names you will remember later. Optional login email is added to workspace mailboxes and linked to the identity.
onboarding.identityVsEmailShort: Identity = who. Login email = which address they use (stored once per workspace, linkable from assets too).
onboarding.identityLoginEmailHint: If set, Hilko creates or reuses this address under Email addresses and links it to this identity.
onboarding.reviewHint: We create the project, identities you listed, and optional placeholder assets. Nothing secret is stored.
onboarding.noProvidersSelected: No providers — you can add assets from the inventory later.
onboarding.errorProjectName: Enter a project name to continue.
onboarding.stepNavNeedProject: Name your project (step 2) before jumping ahead.
onboarding.errorFinalize: Could not finish setup. Try again.
onboarding.resourcesHint: One screen per item: name, type (including Other), identity, login email, role, and verification.
onboarding.resourcesEmpty: Pick tools on the previous step or add an Other resource.
onboarding.assetsHint: Each provider becomes an asset row — e.g. GitHub login vs main repo are different names and types.
onboarding.assetAccessHint: One screen per enabled resource — assign who manages it and mark verification now so the project checklist stays short.
onboarding.assetAccessNoAssets: Enable at least one resource on the previous step.
onboarding.assetAccessSkip: Skip access for this resource (no role)
onboarding.assetAccessNoIdentities: Add a sign-in identity on step 4, or skip access here.
onboarding.assetAccessLinkEmail: Also link login email {email} to this resource
onboarding.assetAccessVerifyDeclaredHint: In inventory for now — confirm later in the asset tab.
onboarding.assetAccessVerifyConfirmedHint: You opened the console or DNS and confirm control (saved on this asset).
onboarding.connectionsHint: Optional links between resources (DNS, hosting, deploy).
onboarding.connectionsAccessHint: Creates an asset role (who can administer the resource).
onboarding.connectionsAccessEmpty: Add identities and enabled assets on previous steps to see links here.
onboarding.connectionsDepsHint: Common edges when tools share login or DNS/mail flows — adjust later on the project map.
onboarding.connectionsDepsEmpty: Pick more related providers (e.g. DNS + registrar) to see suggestions.
onboarding.reviewNextStepsHint: You land on the project with next steps — confirm assets, finish links, document dependencies, then verify.
